findings.finding: The executed capex runs at about half of management's guide, and the table's own scenario conditions say the opposite of the numbers. Guide: FY2026 capex is 'approximately $20 billion' (call) or 'in excess of $20 billion' (10-Q). Nine-month capex was 13,014M, so Q4 2026 needs at least about 7.0B. The CFO said capex 'for the next few years would continue to expand' (Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar, compute, a semiconductor fab). The executed capex (maintenance_capex + growth_capex) is: stub 2026-10-27..12-31 bear 3.69B, base 2.46B, bull 1.89B; FY2027 bear 5.5B, base 10.8B, bull 12.6B; FY2028 bear 5.4B, base 11.7B, bull 15.5B. Bear growth capex is zero in 2027-2028. The base condition in table_he.md says investment keeps rising until the new products sell ('about 20bn in 2026'), and the bear condition says R&D and investment keep rising. The executed paths cut capex roughly in half (base) or by three quarters (bear). The deviation from the guide is not stated anywhere: the sales_to_capital reason mentions the 20bn but not that the paths spend about half of it. In FY2027 alone, base free cash flow is overstated by about 9B even if capex only stays at the 2026 level. That is about twice the base FY2027 after-tax operating profit (~4.7B). Holding capex at even 20B a year through 2028 would cut the fair value (38.9) by roughly 10-20%. CLAUDE.md requires forecasts to be linked to investment and funding.
findings.where: companies/TSLA/inputs.json forecast.overrides sales_to_capital (bear 0.8 / base 1.5 / bull 2.5); casefile val.result.scenarios[bear|base|bull].forecast[0..2] maintenance_capex + growth_capex; guidance dc_g_capex_fy2026_oct_call, dc_g_capex_fy2026_oct_10q, fact dc_capex_9m_2026, CFO statement in dc_call_20261021; inputs.json analyst_sheet.scenario_events.base[3] and .bear[1]; out/table_he.md base and bear condition lines
findings.fix: Choose one and rerun ticker-value. (a) Make the executed reinvestment follow the guide: Q4 2026 at about 7.0B, and 2027-2028 at least the 2026 level as the CFO says. For example, use an early-years sales_to_capital near the company's own current reading (fc.anchors.sales_to_capital.history 0.62; FY2026 about 0.8 on the guide) that fades to the scenario values, and say where the extra revenue from that capital lands. (b) Keep the levers, but state next to the result that every path invests about half the guided capex, and rewrite the base and bear conditions (scenario_events base[3], bear[1]) so they match the executed numbers.

findings.finding: The bear funding condition is not executed. The table's bear line (scenario_events.bear[1]) says free cash flow stays thin and the company needs the $30B credit lines, and the 10-Q says heightened capex 'will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow'. The executed bear is status self_funded with zero debt draws, zero equity and only 229M of investments liquidated, because its capex falls to maintenance (5.5B a year). The table shows a condition the bear value does not carry.
findings.where: casefile fc.funding.bear (draws [], investments_liquidated 229,175,232); inputs.json analyst_sheet.scenario_events.bear[1] (evidence dc_credit_unused_commitments_q3_2026); out/table_he.md bear line
findings.fix: After the capex fix above, let the bear draw on cash or the facilities as its executed cash flow requires, and quote the draw. Otherwise drop the credit-line clause from the bear condition.

findings.finding: The share count counts the unearned 2025 CEO award twice. Every scenario values per share on 3,952,757,946 cover shares, which include 423,743,904 unearned 2025 CEO Performance Award restricted shares. Each of the award's 12 tranches needs both a market-capitalization milestone and an operational milestone (10-Q award note). The forecast also carries the award's expense: 275M in Q3 2026 and 802M over nine months, about a quarter of quarterly SBC, with 9.74B probable still unrecognized. That expense sits inside the 4.15% SBC-to-revenue rate charged in every year (fc.anchors.sbc_pct; sbc is also a lever on engine rules). Without the unearned shares, the base value would be about 43.6 instead of 38.9 (x 3,953/3,529). The ~286.5M restricted shares from the exercised 2018 award are earned and correctly counted. This is the same issue review_trace raised; it carries over here because the table's fair value, buy-below and yearly prices all depend on it.
findings.where: casefile val.case.opening.shares and qa.resolved.shares_outstanding (3,952,757,946); fc.anchors.sbc_pct 0.0415 and fc.paths.*.sbc_pct; evidence dc_ceo_award_2025_shares, dc_sbc_ceo_award_q3_2026, dc_sbc_ceo_award_unrecognized_probable, dc_shares_out_20261015
findings.fix: Choose one treatment and state it beside the result. Either count the 423.7M award shares and take the award's SBC out of the forecast SBC rate, or leave the unearned shares out and keep that SBC as a cost (probable versus not-probable split). Read the award's market-cap milestones in the 10-Q or proxy against each scenario's equity value: base 38.9 x 3.95B is about 154B.

findings.finding: The equity bridge leaves out a non-operating investment. dataqa set long_term_investments to 0 'only provisionally', because the line is untagged at 2026-09-30 (674M at 2026-06-30). The 10-Q (traced by review_trace) carries the SpaceX stake at 2,865M fair value (2,002M cost). Neither number is in val.case.opening. That is about 0.72 per share, or 1.9% of the base value.
findings.where: casefile qa.fields.cash_and_liquid_investments note; qa.resolved.long_term_investments (0, no source); val.case.opening; documents facts for the SpaceX fair value and cost (10-Q 2026-10-22)
findings.fix: Confirm the balance-sheet line in the 10-Q and add the stake as a non-operating asset at fair value, kept apart from spendable cash. Otherwise state the omission next to the result.

findings.finding: The yearly table and the fair value use different returns on new capital in the bear and bull scenarios. The DCF's own return on new capital is mature margin x (1 - tax 15%) x sales_to_capital: bear about 3.4%, base 11.5%, bull 31.9%. The company_path economics ROIC is 6%, 12% and 20%. The base agrees. The bear yearly prices assume a better return than the bear DCF, and the bull prices a worse one.
findings.where: inputs.json company_path.scenarios.bear.roic 0.06 and .bull.roic 0.20 against forecast.overrides mature_margin and sales_to_capital (bear 0.05 / 0.8, bull 0.15 / 2.5); casefile fc.anchors.tax.used 0.15
findings.fix: Align the bear and bull economics ROIC with the forecast levers, or say in the scenario reasons why they differ.
